question.text: A reaction of cobalt <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>III</mi><mo>)</mo></math> chloride and ethylenediamine in a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn></math> mole ratio generates two isomeric products <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> (violet-coloured) and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> (green-coloured). <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> can show optical activity, but, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> is optically inactive. What type of isomers do <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> represent?

solution.text:
The coordination number of cobalt is 6.

The mole ratio of CoCl3 and en is 1 : 2.

Hence,

CoCl3+2 en→Coen2Cl2 Cl

The complex formed shows geometrical isomerism.

The complex exists as cis and trans isomers among which the trans isomer is optically inactive.
